name: ADUM263N1BRIZ-RL
title: 5.0 kV rms six-channel digital isolators
summary: ADuM260N, ADuM261N, ADuM262N and ADuM263N: six-channel digital isolators in a 16-lead wide-body SOIC_IC with 5 kV rms withstand, carrying logic over an on/off-keyed transformer barrier. The models split the six channels 6/0, 5/1, 4/2 and 3/3 between the two directions. Each side runs from 1.7 V to 5.5 V, so the part also translates levels; data rate is at least 150 Mbps and delay at most 13 ns at 5 V. N0 versions fall to low and N1 versions to high when the input side loses power.
key_figures: 5000 V rms for 1 min (UL 1577); VIORM 849 V peak
1.7 V to 5.5 V on each side
13 ns max at 5 V, 15 ns max at 1.8 V

circuits.title: Recommended PCB layout
circuits.description: The ADuM263N with a decoupling capacitor on each supply and no other parts: C1 across VDD1 and GND1 (pins 1 and 8), C2 across VDD2 and GND2 (pins 16 and 9). Channels A to C enter on side 1 and leave on side 2, channels D to F enter on side 2 and leave on side 1, each wired straight to its logic. Each capacitor is 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF, with its two leads together no more than 10 mm long to the supply pin.

notes: The ADuM260N, ADuM261N and ADuM262N take the same two capacitors on the same pins; their channel directions follow their own pinouts.

operation.text: Six-channel digital isolators rated 5.0 kV rms, all in one 16-lead wide-body SOIC_IC. The four models differ in how many channels run each way: ADuM260N six from side 1 to side 2; ADuM261N five forward, one back; ADuM262N four and two; ADuM263N three and three. The digit after N gives the fail-safe level: N0 outputs go low, N1 outputs go high when the input side has no power.

Each channel sends a high-frequency carrier through chip-scale transformer coils with polyimide layers between them, switching the carrier on and off with the data (on/off keying) over a differential path. In N0 models the carrier is off while the input is low; in N1 models it is off while the input is high, so a dead input side reads low or high respectively. Outputs hold the right level at dc with no input edges needed. The carrier is spread-spectrum to cut radiated emissions, and the design aims at high common-mode transient and magnetic-field immunity.

Internal regulators let each side run anywhere from 1.7 V to 5.5 V on its own, so the part shifts logic levels among 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V. Input thresholds and output levels scale with their own side's supply (VDDx). Input edges may be as slow as 1.0 ms.

Each supply has a lockout with typical thresholds of 1.6 V rising and 1.5 V falling, 0.1 V hysteresis. A powered output whose input side is unpowered sits at its fail-safe level; an unpowered output side is indeterminate.
Keep logic inputs low on a side whose supply is off; a high input there powers the part through its ESD structures.

The logic pins need no interface parts. Bypass both supplies: VDD1 with a capacitor from pin 1 to pin 8, VDD2 with one from pin 16 to pin 9, each 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF. The combined lead length from both capacitor ends to the supply pin is 10 mm at most. Application note AN-1109 gives further layout guidance.

Large common-mode transients call for minimal board coupling across the barrier, shared equally by all pins of a side. Uneven coupling drives pin-to-pin voltages past the absolute maximum ratings, causing latch-up or permanent damage.

tPLH (output going high) and tPHL (output going low) are each measured from the input's 50% point to the output's 50% point and need not be equal; their largest difference is the pulse width distortion. Channel matching is the largest delay spread among the channels of one part; propagation delay skew is the largest delay spread among separate parts under identical conditions.

Jitter comes from an eye diagram taken at 150 Mbps with a pseudorandom bit sequence 2(n − 1), n = 14, 5 V supplies, on a 1 GHz, 10 GSPS oscilloscope with jitter analysis; a typical part shows 490 ps p-p.

Insulation degrades in two ways. Surface tracking sets creepage in system standards from the total rms working voltage, pollution degree and material group; this package is material group II with 8.3 mm creepage. Wear-out comes from displacement current in the polyimide and depends on thickness, material and voltage stress; dc adds almost none, so only the ac rms part of the barrier voltage sets lifetime. The ac limits of the maximum continuous working voltage table apply to that ac part; its dc limit comes from package creepage under IEC 60664-1 and may differ under a particular system standard.

The W in a model name marks automotive qualification. ADuM262N1WBRIZ and ADuM262N1WBRIZ-RL (misprinted ADuM262N1BRIZ-RL) are built under controlled manufacturing for automotive quality and reliability, and their specifications may differ from those of the commercial models.
16-lead wide-body SOIC with increased creepage (SOIC_IC, RI-16-2), RoHS compliant, JEDEC MS-013-AC. Dimensions in millimetres.
